text:
Ava M: Hi team - I had a 20-week ultrasound at an outpatient imaging center and the EOB shows it as out-of-network. Provider said they'd billed under the hospital taxonomy. I'm 28 weeks and this is for routine prenatal screening. Any ideas?
Benefits Team: Sorry that's stressful. Did the imaging center give you a facility vs professional charge split? Sometimes the tech is in-network but the facility isn't.
Ava M: The bill PDF is attached: https://redwood-cloud/internal-uploads/claims/1825102345-ultrasound-bill.pdf It lists CPT 76805 and has two line items: facility charge $650, tech fee $120. The front desk insisted they were in the hospital system.
benefits-bot: Automated guidance: Routine prenatal ultrasounds are covered under Basic Care B when performed by in-network facility/providers. If billed out-of-network, member may be eligible for balance billing protection if the service was scheduled through an in-network OB/GYN.
Priya S: Can you confirm the scheduling clinic/ordering provider? If your OB ordered it, that helps for prior auth/appeal. Also please DM the provider's NPI if you have it.
Ava M: OB is Dr. Chen at Midtown OB (in-network). Appointment was scheduled through their office. I don't have the NPI handy.
Carrier Liaison: If the ordering provider is in-network and the imaging location is part of the same hospital system, carrier can reprocess under network rates. Please send the order and scheduling confirmation to benefits@redwood.com.
Ava M: Sent order PDF and scheduling email thread. Subject: "Prenatal ultrasound appeal - Ava M - 03/06/2026"
Benefits Team: Received and opened case #BR-8523. We'll submit a reconsideration to Atlas Health citing coordinated care and scheduling by in-network OB.
Priya S: Timeline: we'll file within 1 business day; carrier response usually 10-15 business days. If denied, next step is formal appeal attaching scheduling confirmation and a statement from your OB that this was part of routine prenatal care.
Ava M: Quick Q: will I need to pay the balance while this is pending?
Benefits Team: Typically carrier may place the balance on hold if we request reprocessing. However, billing cycles vary. You can call the billing department and inform them the claim is under appeal; request a hold or ask for an itemized statement with a hold code. Save all correspondence.
Ava M: Called billing, they put a 30-day hold and gave me a reference number. Thanks.
Carrier Liaison: Noted. We'll include billing hold reference in the appeal packet. If the facility insists on balance billing after carrier reversal, we can escalate to surrogate billing team.
Ava M: Appreciate it. One last thing 1 if carrier denies, can I get help from benefits to negotiate?
Benefits Team: Yes. If denial stands, Benefits will assist with escalation and, if applicable, balance-billing protections (state regulations) and arbitration steps. We'll loop you back once we hear.
Ava M: Thank you all! :heart:
